name: Vardhman Special Steels Ltd
title: Vardhman Special Steels Ltd - 534392 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Vardhman Special Steels posted record FY26 profit of about INR122 crore on 225,000 tons volume; EBITDA/ton guidance raised to INR8,000-11,000.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a record year, with profit of about INR122 crore and sales volume of 225,000 tons, in line with budget. The Iran-US conflict pushed raw material prices up in Q4 and raised gas costs, but gas supply was not disrupted. Management raised FY27 EBITDA/ton guidance to INR8,000-11,000 from INR7,000-10,000 and set a 2-year target of INR9,000-12,000. The call centred on a reheating furnace commissioned in March, a solar plant, a new 210x210 section, a forging project, and a planned greenfield steel plant with capex of about INR2,000 crore.

segments.name: Automotive special steels (existing plant)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume 225,000 tons; FY27 sales target about 250,000-255,000 tons, with 250,000 tons to be used for modelling. Rolling capacity about 180,000 tons was supplemented by outsourced rolling; rolling capacity rises to 270,000 tons after the reheating furnace.

segments.name: Forging (ring gears, Aichi technology)
segments.commentary: Project budget INR475 crore, now expected to come in below that; about INR80 crore spent so far. First line targeted for Jan-Mar 2028 start, with ramp-up in FY29; plans for at least 3 lines.

segments.name: Greenfield steel plant
segments.commentary: Capacity 500,000-600,000 tons; commissioning targeted July 2029; land acquisition expected to close in May 2026. Ramp-up budgeted at 5-6 years to full utilisation.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA/ton guidance INR8,000-11,000; INR9,000-12,000 targeted in about 2 years, with management saying this could be a more confident range.
FY27 rolled volume target about 250,000-255,000 tons; for modelling, management asked analysts to use 250,000 tons, with a static 270,000-275,000 tons thereafter for the existing plant.

Melt shop currently under 300,000 tons licence; expansion to about 360,000 tons needs environmental clearance (50-50 chance, decision expected before March 2027); if approved, commissioning late CY27.
Price increases sought from Q1 FY27 to pass through higher scrap costs; discussions ongoing.
Government incentives expected at about INR12-13 crore in FY27, as the GST refund scheme ends Aug 2026 and electricity duty exemption runs to Aug 2029.
Equity infusion of about INR1,200 crore (INR385 crore already in, about INR800 crore to come), plus about INR1,200 crore debt; peak debt/equity below 0.75, comfort at 0.5.
capex_capacity: Reheating furnace commissioned March 2026, lifting rolling capacity to 270,000 tons; 9 crore units/year solar plant commissioned in Q4; new 210x210 section added to improve cast productivity and reduce rework.
Heat size raised from 37 tons to 40 tons; new NDT line and new peeling line in progress; Kocks Block commissioned.
Melt shop: plan to raise melting from 300,000 to about 360,000 tons, subject to environmental approval; equipment lead time 1-1.5 years.

Capex FY27 about INR100 crore (mostly land and development for the new plant, plus normal/replacement capex); FY27-28 expansion capex about INR700-800 crore, plus about INR100 crore for the existing plant and INR80-100 crore more if environmental approval comes.

Committed investment about INR2,600 crore through FY30: about INR2,000 crore for the steel plant and INR475 crore for forging; further specialised-alloy investments (ESR, VAR, VIM) still to be planned.
demand_pricing: Pricing works on spreads, not commodity prices; alloy steel prices rise less than commodity steel when scrap rises and fall less when scrap falls. Management said average selling price fell in FY26 versus FY25 despite higher volume.
Exports to be mainly indirect, via components from India to global OEs and EU FTA/CBAM benefits; direct export share to stay low. Luxury OEs such as BMW and Mercedes-Benz may give better prices.
Forging customer validation: Maruti Suzuki wants to see the factory running before validation; Aichi-linked approvals may be faster.
Management sees tool and die steel imports of about INR1,000 crore/year as an opportunity for future ingot-casting products.
Product mix expected to stay similar for the foreseeable future; a dip is likely when the new plant ramps up.

qa_highlights.question: What volume should be modelled for rolled products and is 250,000 tons sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said keep 250,000 tons for FY27 (target 255,000), with 270,000-275,000 tons from the following year and static at that level for existing plant modelling.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA/ton be in the 8,500-11,000 range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed guidance of INR8,000-11,000 for this year, moving to INR9,000-12,000 in about 2 years; FY26 averaged above INR8,500.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakup of FY26 capex and how much will the forging project cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Kocks Block, reheating furnace, warehouses and land were the main items. Forging budget INR475 crore, spend so far about INR80 crore; expected to finish below budget, with more precise figures in about 6 months.

qa_highlights.question: What are the expected FY27/FY28 capex and funding plans?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex about INR100 crore; FY27-28 about INR700-800 crore for expansion. Debt/equity to stay below 0.75; about INR1,200 crore equity (INR385 crore in, Vardhman Group INR300-400 crore, Aichi, possible QIP) and about INR1,200 crore debt.

qa_highlights.question: What are government incentives and will the new plant get PLI?
qa_highlights.answer: No PLI for the new plant; it will be under the Punjab scheme. Incentives about INR12-13 crore in FY27 versus INR24 crore in FY26, as the GST refund ends Aug 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What ROCE is expected after the new plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management hopes EBITDA on capital employed stays above 20% once plants reach full utilisation; below 20% it would not make sense to keep investing.

qa_highlights.question: What components will the forging plant make and what is its capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Ring gears for cars, using an Aichi process; one line initially versus Aichi's 9 lines. Management declined to give asset-level detail.

risks_watch: Environmental approval for the melt shop expansion to 360,000 tons is uncertain (management puts it at 50-50); Ludhiana is in a critically polluted zone.
Forging ramp-up depends on customer validation; Maruti Suzuki will validate only after seeing the factory operating; FY29 is the first year of meaningful forging volume.
Greenfield plant timeline (July 2029) and 5-6 year ramp-up carry execution and cost risk; capex figures are described as rough ballpark estimates.
Raw material and gas cost volatility from the Iran-US conflict; management flagged possible global recession and high oil prices as factors affecting the EBITDA range.
Dilution and funding: about INR800 crore equity still to come, including a possible QIP, and about INR1,200 crore debt to raise.
Expiry of the GST refund incentive in Aug 2026 lowers FY27 subsidy income to about INR12-13 crore.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on volume, EBITDA range and the new plants, but cautious on specific numbers: capex, environmental approval and the forging ramp are repeatedly described as rough or ballpark. Management avoided project-level returns and firm timelines beyond FY28.
key_quotes: So this year, our guidance is now up from last year, which is INR8,000 to INR11,000 a ton EBITDA.
So we are very clear, we will remain only in the area of special steels and automotive forgings.
So after the plants are established and running towards full capacity utilization, EBITDA on capital employed, we hope to continue to be above 20%.
